papers.title_en: Representation Learning via Composite Subspace Flow Matching
papers.evidence: 用于表示学习的复合子空间流匹配
papers.tldr: 自监督表示学习常在判别性与生成性间取舍：联合嵌入丢弃类内方差，生成模型易被像素变化主导。CSFM把表示学习视为跨光谱、颜色与光照子空间的确定性退化课程的可逆反演，并用硬时序风格截断约束轨迹方差。在CIFAR-10/100和STL-10上，它在CNN与ViT中兼顾判别迁移和生成合成，线性探针与少样本分类优于标准最优传输流。结果表明，引导生成流的物理动力学可学得线性可分且可生成反演的表示。
papers.abstract_en: Distilling semantic meaning from raw image data remains a challenge in machine learning. Current self-supervised paradigms face a trade-off: joint-embedding architectures produce relevant features by aggressively discarding intra-class variance, irreversibly spatial and reconstruction. Conversely, generative models preserve spatial details but struggle to isolate semantics, as their optimization is dominated by pixel variations. To bridge this divide, we propose composite subspace flow matching (CSFM). Rather than corrupting data with unstructured isotropic noise, CSFM formulates representation learning as the variance-minimizing inversion of a deterministic degradation curriculum across spectral, color, and illumination subspaces. By bounding trajectory variance with hard temporal style truncation, a capacity-constrained encoder is driven to ignore transient style artifacts and encode persistent content. Empirical evaluations across CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and STL-10 show that CSFM yields competitive discriminative transferability while preserving generative synthesis across both convolutional and vision transformer architectures. By avoiding the collapse pathologies of non-generative methods, CSFM forms a smooth latent space that outperforms standard optimal transport flows on linear probing and few-shot classification, while enabling coherent synthesis and trajectory interpolation. These results confirm that steering the physical dynamics of generative flows offers a scalable paradigm for learning representations that are simultaneously linearly separable and generatively invertible.

papers.title_en: PRIME W0: Physical Priors from World Models for Embodied Manipulation
papers.authors: Huabin Peng, Fagang Jin, Yancong Wei, Tengfei Ma, Chuhang Liu, Chao Yu, Liqing Chen
papers.evidence: 面向具身动作的分层条件流匹配
papers.tldr: 现有视觉-语言-动作模型多以前馈方式仅根据当前观测预测动作，既丢失长时程时序上下文，也未充分利用VLM的层级表征。PRIME W0提出分层条件流匹配框架，通过逐层KV注入、自适应MoE动作专家、世界模型异步子目标图像预测与DINOv2历史帧语义桥，并采用协方差结构化噪声的Action Dynamic Manifold流匹配尊重机器人运动学耦合。该模型经四阶段训练，在LIBERO和真实机器人基准取得SOTA，系统消融验证各架构组件有效。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models excel at instruction following, yet most remain feed-forward: they condition actions only on the current observation and discard both long-horizon temporal context and the hierarchical structure of VLM representations. We present PRIME W0, a hierarchical conditional flow-matching framework that closes this gap through three synergistic designs: (1)per-layer KV injection from a pretrained VLM into an Adaptive MoE action expert; (2)dynamics-aware conditioning via asynchronous world-model subgoal-image prediction and a DINOv2 historical-frame semantic bridge; and (3)Action Dynamic Manifold (ADM) flow matching with covariance-structured noise that respects robot kinematic coupling. PRIME W0 is trained in four stages---VLM pre-training, DAT/NTP visuomotor pre-training, DiT flow-matching decoder assembly with WM injection, and end-to-end SFT---and achieves state-of-the-art results on LIBERO and real-robot benchmarks, with systematic ablations validating each architectural component.

papers.title_en: Learning Safe Flow Matching Robot Policies from Binary Feasibility Oracles
papers.authors: Jianming Ma, Rongjun Jin, Yizhi Chen, Yue Gao
papers.evidence: 面向安全流匹配机器人策略的预言机引导防护
papers.tldr: 机器人基础模型常用流匹配生成动作，但难以保证关节限位与避障等物理约束，尤其可行域只能通过黑盒二元可行性预言机查询。本文提出预言机引导的可微安全护栏，在前向用二元查询纠正不安全更新，反向提取局部边界信息形成约束感知学习信号，并与离散时间流匹配结合，使训练与推理共用同一护栏。实验在障碍感知操作任务中实现100%约束满足，同时保持任务性能，为仅有可行性查询的安全机器人策略学习提供了实用方案。
papers.abstract_en: Robot foundation models increasingly rely on flow-based action generation for general-purpose manipulation, yet the generated actions are not guaranteed to satisfy physical constraints such as joint limits and collision avoidance. This problem is especially challenging when the feasible set cannot be described analytically and is accessible only through black-box feasibility oracles. We study this practical oracle-only setting and propose an oracle-guided differentiable safeguard for safe flow-matching robot policies. The safeguard uses binary feasibility queries to correct unsafe updates in the forward pass, while extracting local boundary information to provide constraint-aware learning signals in the backward pass. Combined with discrete-time flow matching, the same safeguard is used during training and inference, enabling forward--backward aligned policy learning without explicit or differentiable constraint models. Experiments on obstacle-aware robotic manipulation demonstrate 100% constraint satisfaction while preserving task performance.
